newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NAB hits profit wall.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NAB hits profit wall.

text.p: Australia's largest bank and its most profitable listed company, National Australia Bank (NAB) Ltd, posted a surprise 9.5-percent profit drop in the third quarter on Thursday.
The profit slide shocked a market used to steadily rising profits from NAB, sparking a market-wide selloff and forcing many to re-evaluate their outlooks for the banking sector.

NAB has warned for a year that a price war in the key home mortgage market would slice into Australian lending margins to lower and flatten profits, but strong performances in the last two quarters had soothed market fears.
NAB's net profit fell to A$504 million (US$368 million) in the three months to June 30 from A$557 million in the March quarter and A$505 million in the June quarter of 1996.
Analysts had forecast a quarterly net profit of about A$545 million, buoyed by prospects of strong overseas earnings and NAB's ability to cut costs and generate non-interest income.
Instead National Australia Bank's stronger British and European earnings were more than overwhelmed by a 15-percent slump in Australian profits.

NAB's Australian operations contributed profit of A$292 million in the June quarter, down 15.3 percent from the A$345 million posted in the March quarter and down 6.7 percent from the A$313 million posted in the same quarter a year earlier.
Profits from NAB's New Zealand unit, Bank of New Zealand, fell to A$44 million from A$47 million in the March quarter and A$51 million in the June quarter of 1996.

The best performing units in NAB's global group were the British and European units. Their profits rose 36 percent to A$132 million between the June quarters of 1996 and 1997, due in part to a strong British pound.
Brokers and analysts were disappointed with overall result.
"The NAB result was about A$50 million below expectations for the quarter," said BNP Equities Head of Equities John Bowie Wilson.
"It looks like the first chink in the armour for the banking stocks that we've seen. The whole banking sector has suffered because of it," Bowie Wilson said.
Analysts said they were looking to cut full-year forecasts by up to A$100 million for the year ending September.
Previous forecasts of NAB's full-year earnings had ranged from A$2.22 billion to A$2.29 billion.
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett analyst Mike Pulman lowered his full year forecast to A$2.157 billion from A$2.25 billion.
"I think the last quarter will be marginally better (than the third quarter). Margins should continue to be squeezed and the bad debt provision may be up slightly," Pulman said.
NAB's shares slid 50 cents or over 2.5 percent to A$19.00 in a hectic first half hour of trade after the results.
Other bank stocks, which have raced ahead of the market with NAB in the last six months, also eased back. The banking index fell about one percent.
